en.html:
...One hit would decide it.

That was how I read the situation.

The Silver Star could destroy me—Muramasa—with a single blow. No need to explain that part.
But the reverse was true too. She was no longer that enormous god. This body was small enough for one sweep of a sword to cut through.

Whoever landed the hit, won.

Not a fight on the ground, but close enough to one. We were floating under gravity control, near enough to speak in our own voices. That was where the fight would begin.

To change over to flight now would be the same as turning my back on her and running. A fatal opening, handed over personally.

Don't move.
When you move, attack.

One blow that puts the enemy down. Nothing less.

……勝負は一撃。
　
　そう、見て取る。

　言わずもがな、銀星号は<ruby>村正<rt>おれ</rt></ruby>を一打で撃破可能だ。
　そして逆も然り。銀星号は既に大巨躯の〝神〟では
なく、剣の一薙で裁断される<ruby>規模<rt>サイズ</rt></ruby>に過ぎない。

　一撃、当てた方が勝つ。

　戦闘状況は、地上戦ではないが、地上戦に近い。
　互いに重力制御で浮遊したこの格好、肉声の対話が
できるこの間合を、始点としたためだ。

　今から騎航に移るのは、敵前で背を見せて逃げるも
同然。
　致命的な隙となる。

　動いてはならない。
　動く時は、攻める時。

　必倒の一打を対敵に放つ時。

The Silver Star held her left hand forward, right hand drawn back.

Enju. One of the unarmed guards of the Yoshino Style Rules of Engagement.
A little altered to suit herself.

The left hand defends or makes a feint, neutralizes the enemy's attack; then the right hand wins the exchange. That is what Enju is meant to do.
But this particular user was hardly going to obey the guard's instruction manual.

Most likely...

en.html:
The same thing she had done above Hachiman Shrine.
No little tricks. Come straight at me, with speed alone to depend on.

Ordinarily, such a headlong rush hardly deserves to be called a tactic.
But when the fighting speed goes beyond what you can even perceive, all your clever tactics may stand aside. That rush is more frightening than any of them.

And then a punch—or a kick.
Either would do. That strength, that skill, and now anger and the intent to kill behind them: fist or foot, she could scatter me together with my armour.

en.html:
On my side,
I raised the nodachi above my right shoulder.

The orthodox high guard of an armoured warrior. Looks simple, contains a thousand variations, ends in the same thing: the enemy comes within reach, you cut.

Bas. That much.

I could put a trick into it, certainly. Against this opponent, better not to show my cleverness.
If it merely went to waste, that would be good luck. It could eat up time worth more than gold and make losing a certainty.

When we crossed, there would be no allowance for some extra achievement. Assume I could do one thing only: cut.

Catch the Silver Star at the instant she enters reach. Cut.

...That was all the technique I should attempt.

Reach, at least, was in my favour.
She had no weapon. I had the nodachi. My striking distance was much greater.

I could wait for her to move and STILL strike first.

—Provided.

Provided I caught the exact instant she entered my range. Provided her speed did not leave me behind before I could act.

That was where winning and losing separated.
Could I seize that instant? This thing I had never managed, not once—could I do it NOW...?

ja.html:
対して。
　俺は、野太刀を右肩上に構える。

　武者正調、上段の太刀取り。
　単純と見えて千変万化の幅を持つが、その帰結する
ところはやはり単一である――間合に入った敵を斬る。

　それだけだ。

　細工を仕込むのも可能だが、相手を思えば、やらぬ
方がましなくらいであろう。
　無駄、で済むならむしろ僥倖。千金より貴重な時間
を食い潰し、敗北を決定付ける要因となり得る。

　やがて訪れる交錯の間、<ruby>ただ斬る<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>以上の何かをする
余裕など無いと見るべきだ。

　銀星号が間合に踏み込む瞬間を捉えて斬る。
　
　……俺が行使する術技は、これのみとするが正しい。

　<ruby>此方<rt>こちら</rt></ruby>には間合の利がある。
　無手の敵に対し、野太刀を扱う俺は攻撃範囲の点で
大きく優っている。

　敵が動くのを待った上で先制する事ができるのだ。

　――但し。
　
　間合に入る瞬間を、<ruby>確<rt>しか</rt></ruby>と掴めるのならばである。
　銀星号の速度に振り切られてしまうことなく。

　ここが勝敗を分ける最重要点。
　俺はその機を<ruby>もの<rt>・・</rt></ruby>にできるか？　嘗て一度たりとも
成功していない大難業を、今こそ果たせるのか……？

The Silver Star's breathing remained perfectly calm.

As though asleep—
No. She WAS asleep.

She was a dream.

And a dream's stillness of spirit could reach the realm of gods and immortals.

—True dream-swordsmanship.

How was I to catch that first instant and take control of it?

Three conditions. If I wanted to succeed, to win, all three.

One.
Do not forget that the enemy is the Silver Star.

One.
Forget that the enemy is Hikaru Minato.

銀星号の呼吸は何処までも鎮静である。

　<ruby>恰<rt>あたか</rt></ruby>も眠れる者の如し――
　否、眠れる者そのもの。

　あれは夢である。

　夢なれば、心気の静謐なるは神仙の域に届く。
　
　――正真の夢想剣。

　この機先を、如何にして掴み制するか。

　成功と勝利の条件は三つだ。

　一つ。
　敵は<ruby>銀星号<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>である事を忘れない。

　一つ。
　敵は<ruby>湊斗光<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>である事を忘れる。

en.html:
When my mind was contaminated...
I had used a sword stroke I could never ordinarily manage.

Split armour without relying on a tsurugi's power. That impossible thing, I had done it.

The stroke had come from the state of my mind. The contamination had forced it into one rigid purpose.
Not no-self. The opposite of no-self. But all other thoughts had been driven out, and in THAT respect it was the same.

From that state, the stroke had come.

...Yes. And even before that, long ago—when I had used the same stroke, my mind had been like that too.

If I could reach no-self, or something close to it, then that level of technique was within my reach.
Defeating the Silver Star, also.

If I could get my mind there...

en.html: Face to face. No more than a breath between us. The time a needle takes to pass through one thin sheet of paper. That was all. Our eyes met. The fight was decided. I had taken the moment as far as it could go. Made the fastest cut, by the shortest path. And still it was not enough. This speed. Still I could not get beyond it. One thousandth of an instant more would have done. Only that much. I could have cut her before she reached me. But that much also, the Silver Star would not give. Already inside my guard. Too close for the long nodachi to cut, however much I wanted it to. Close enough that her fist could not miss. Close enough to kill for certain. From here, there was no turning it around. Winning and losing were decided. —Decided, no? Then—◆ what was my body STILL DOING?
en.text:
Face to face. No more than a breath between us.

The time a needle takes to pass through one thin sheet of paper. That was all.
Our eyes met.

The fight was decided.

I had taken the moment as far as it could go.
Made the fastest cut, by the shortest path.

And still it was not enough.

This speed.
Still I could not get beyond it.

One thousandth of an instant more would have done. Only that much. I could have cut her before she reached me.

But that much also, the Silver Star would not give.

Already inside my guard.

Too close for the long nodachi to cut, however much I wanted it to.

Close enough that her fist could not miss. Close enough to kill for certain.

From here, there was no turning it around.

Winning and losing were decided.

—Decided, no?

Then—◆
what was my body STILL DOING?

ja.html: 接吻を交わす程の間で、見合う。 　薄紙一枚を針で貫く――それだけの時刻。 　視線と視線を交わす。 　勝負は決した。 　戦機を極めに極め。 　最速の剣、最短の剣を為し。 　遂に及ばぬ。 　この速度。 　遂に超えられぬ。 　あと一瞬の千分の一、時間があれば良かった。 　それだけあれば、敵が襲う前に斬れた。 　だがその寸暇を、この白銀は与えなかった。 　間合は既に懐。 　長尺の野太刀では斬りとうても斬れぬ距離。 　敵の拳打は決して外さぬ必殺の距離。 　かくなれば趨勢、もはや覆らぬ。 　勝敗は決した。 　――決したのだ。 　ならば、◆ 　俺は・・、何をしているのか・・・・・・・・。
ja.text:
接吻を交わす程の間で、見合う。

　薄紙一枚を針で貫く――それだけの時刻。
　視線と視線を交わす。

　勝負は決した。

　戦機を極めに極め。
　最速の剣、最短の剣を為し。

　遂に及ばぬ。

　この速度。
　遂に超えられぬ。

　あと一瞬の千分の一、時間があれば良かった。
　それだけあれば、敵が襲う前に斬れた。

　だがその寸暇を、この白銀は与えなかった。

　間合は既に懐。

　長尺の野太刀では斬りとうても斬れぬ距離。

　敵の拳打は決して外さぬ必殺の距離。

　かくなれば趨勢、もはや覆らぬ。

　勝敗は決した。

　――決したのだ。

　ならば、◆
　俺は・・、何をしているのか・・・・・・・・。

en.html: My right hand was moving. That was strange. It was supposed to be holding the nodachi. Why had it let go? What did it think it was doing? It went toward my waist. Reached to seize something there. There—◆ the short sword.

That was strange.
It was supposed to be holding the nodachi.

Why had it let go?

It went toward my waist.

There—◆
the short sword.

Yoshino Style Rules of Engagement—

—Hiyoku. Paired Wings.

The instant the long sword cuts down, the right hand leaves it, draws the short sword, and cuts upward.

For the enemy who reads the long blade and jumps inside its reach, there is the answer waiting.

Without deciding to.

How was I managing this?
